page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16ms_v2 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the FXmsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The physical layout consists of 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The server features an exceptionally high memory capacity of 1344.0 GB, translating to 84.0 GB of RAM per core. There are no GPUs bundled with this instance, and local storage is listed as none, though the server is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities and memory write performance. The server achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2364.0 and a text processing score of 2950.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth for large-block uncached writes is strong at 91.25 GB/sec, and single-threaded gzip compression reaches 34.83 GB/sec. Multi-core performance, such as the stress-ng multi-core score of 17775.0 and Geekbench multi-core score of 13643.0, falls within the average range.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a highly specialized hardware profile with a massive memory-to-vCPU ratio. This makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel core counts. However, a notable tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, meaning all storage operations must rely on externally attached premium storage, which may impact overall I/O latency.

The FX64-16ms_v2 is suited for memory-intensive applications, large in-memory databases, caching layers, and single-threaded data processing tasks that benefit from high clock speeds and massive RAM capacity. It is also applicable for lightweight LLM inference, where it achieves a strong text generation speed of 282.43 tokens/sec on small 135M models.
